newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mercosur countries launch shipping corridor.
newsitem.headline: Mercosur countries launch shipping corridor.

text.p: Senior port officials from the four member states of the Mercosur customs union have launched an Atlantic shipping corridor which is to connect the countries' major ports with regularly operating shipping lines.

Port directors from Manaus, Belem, Sao Luis, Salvador, Vitoria, Rio de Janeiro, Imbituba, Montevideo, Asuncion, Buenos Aires and Bahia Blanca signed a protocol of intent in Rio de Janeiro Thursday creating the Mercosur Atlantic Corridor.

Paulo Vivacqua, the coordinator for the project, said the aim was to cut transport costs and increase trade by creating an opportunity to move more goods between Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay by sea rather than by road.
He believes transport costs in the region can be reduced by half within five years.
"This maritime transport corridor which transfers goods from roads to ships will link areas which were previously isolated from one another," said Vivacqua.
The project also aims to attract private investment for ports and navigation, and to improve infrastructure linking the ports with the hinterland.

The next step will be to form a non-profit consortium to put the corridor into effect and to create a center for port development to train staff, carry out research and improve technology, Vivacqua said.
The headquarters of Brazil's center-east maritime corridor in the port of Vitoria, of which Vivacqua is president, will coordinate the Mercosur corridor.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
